fit_reason: Eaton makes switchgear, circuit protection, UPS, power distribution assemblies and power quality equipment, which covers grid connection, distribution inside the site and keeping it running. These are the long-lead items whose scarcity and rising power per rack drive the sub-sector's demand, and electrical equipment is Eaton's core business through its two Electrical segments. It is one of the largest suppliers of data center electrical equipment and among the best placed for 800 V DC conversion.

Schneider Electric supplies circuit breakers, medium voltage switchgear, transformers, UPS, IT power distribution and prefabricated data center modules, spanning grid connection, distribution and backup. Demand for this equipment grows with every data center built and with power per rack, and energy management is Schneider's largest division. It is one of the two or three leading global suppliers of data center critical power.

Vertiv makes AC and DC power management for data centers, including Liebert UPS, power distribution, busway and integrated rack systems, so it sits in distributing power inside the site and keeping it running. Its equipment scales with the number of data centers and the power per rack, and data centers are its main market, making the sub-sector central. It is a leading pure-play data center power supplier and is positioned for 800 V DC power conversion.

Hubbell makes electrical distribution, transmission and substation products for utilities plus wiring and electrical products for commercial and industrial buildings, covering grid connection and distribution inside the site. Grid connection equipment is scarce and every new data center needs it, and electrical products are essentially all of Hubbell's business. It is a major US utility and electrical products supplier, though its data center exposure is indirect through utilities and construction.

Quanta Services builds and maintains electric transmission, distribution and substation infrastructure and does commercial and industrial wiring, making it an installer of the equipment that connects sites to the grid. Grid connection is a key constraint on data center buildout and contractors are needed for every site, and electric power infrastructure is Quanta's largest segment. It is the largest US electric infrastructure contractor.

ABB's Electrification segment supplies switchgear, modular substation packages, circuit breakers, UPS and distribution automation, with data centers named among its markets, covering grid connection, distribution and backup. Demand for these products grows with data center construction and rising power per rack, and Electrification is ABB's largest segment alongside motion, robotics and process automation. It is one of the leading global suppliers of low and medium voltage electrical equipment.

Hitachi supplies transformers, switches, breakers, UPS and power grid systems through its energy business, which places it in grid connection and backup. Large power transformers have the longest lead times and are among the scarcest items in the sub-sector, but Hitachi is a diversified conglomerate so electrical equipment is one part of a broad business. Through Hitachi Energy it is one of the largest transformer and grid equipment makers in the world.

GE Vernova's Electrification segment provides grid infrastructure and power conversion technologies, including transformers, switchgear and grid solutions, placing it in grid connection and power conversion. Grid connection equipment is scarce with long lead times as data centers are planned, while its larger gas turbine business belongs to Power rather than this sub-sector. Its Electrification business is a major and fast-growing grid equipment supplier.

Siemens Energy's Grid Technologies unit supplies transformers, HVDC systems, high-voltage substations, gas-insulated switchgear and circuit breakers, which is grid connection and stepping power down. These are the long-lead items that hold up sites, though its gas turbine and wind businesses sit outside this sub-sector. It is one of the largest global suppliers of transformers and high-voltage grid equipment.

Powell Industries designs and builds custom switchgear, power control room substations, medium voltage circuit breakers and bus duct systems, covering grid connection and distribution. Switchgear has lead times of about a year and demand rises with every large site, and electrical apparatus is Powell's entire business. It is a mid-sized specialist historically focused on oil, gas and industrial customers that is less established in data centers.

nVent makes electrical connection and protection products including enclosures, grounding and fastening systems, plus server and network equipment racks, and sells through data center installation specialists, covering distribution and protection inside the site. Rising power per rack adds connection and protection content per rack, and electrical connection and protection is nVent's core business. It is a notable mid-sized supplier with direct data center exposure.

Siemens' Smart Infrastructure segment supplies electrification and electrical products, switchgear and building infrastructure, covering distribution and protection inside the site. Demand grows with data center construction and power per rack, but Siemens is a diversified group where automation, mobility and healthcare are also large. It is a leading global electrical equipment supplier with meaningful data center business.

IES Holdings provides electrical design and construction for facilities including data processing centers, installs data center network infrastructure and manufactures metal-enclosed bus duct and generator enclosures, so it installs and supplies distribution equipment. Contractors and prefabricated equipment are needed to build every data center's power distribution, and electrical work is central to IES. It is a fast-growing mid-sized contractor with significant data center exposure.

MYR Group is an electrical construction contractor building transmission lines, substations and distribution systems for utilities and electrical wiring for commercial and industrial sites including data centers. Installing grid connection and site electrical systems is needed for every data center, and electrical construction is MYR's entire business. It is a mid-sized specialist with exposure to both grid and data center work.

Everus Construction Group builds electrical transmission lines and does internal electrical wiring, cabling and mechanical work, and manufactures electrical control panels, which places it in installing equipment. Electrical contractors are needed for every new site, and electrical and mechanical construction is Everus's core business. It is a smaller regional contractor, so its role in data centers is modest.

Comfort Systems provides mechanical and electrical installation and off-site construction for commercial and industrial buildings, which makes it an electrical contractor and prefabricator. Every data center needs its power installed, but Comfort Systems' mechanical HVAC work is larger than its electrical segment. It is one of the most important contractors in US data center construction.

EMCOR provides electrical construction including power distribution and premise electrical systems, alongside mechanical construction and facilities services, making it an electrical contractor. Electrical contractors are needed to build every data center, and electrical construction is a meaningful but not dominant part of EMCOR's mix. It is one of the largest US electrical and mechanical contractors with substantial data center work.

Generac makes standby generators, including industrial units up to 3,250 kW used as emergency backup for data centers, which is keeping power running. Every data center needs backup generation, and backup power is Generac's core business. Most of its sales are residential, so its position in large data center backup is smaller than the largest generator makers.

Cummins makes standby and prime power generators with paralleling systems and transfer switches through its Power Systems business, which is keeping power running. Data centers need backup generators for every site, but engines and components for trucks and equipment make up most of Cummins' sales. It is one of the largest makers of large data center backup generators.

Vicor makes modular DC-DC converters and power components that convert power at the board and rack level, which is the power conversion that 800 V DC and high-density rack designs need. Rising power per rack and DC designs add conversion content per rack, and power conversion is Vicor's whole business. It is a small specialist whose data center role depends on design wins with accelerator makers.

WEG makes transformers and generators alongside its larger electric motor business, giving it exposure to grid connection equipment. Transformers are scarce with long lead times, but motors and industrial automation are most of WEG's sales. It is a significant and expanding transformer maker outside the largest Western suppliers.

WESCO distributes electrical apparatus, wire and cable, transformers, switches and protective devices to contractors, utilities and data center builders. Distribution is how much of this equipment reaches sites as data centers are built, and electrical distribution is its core though it does not make the equipment. It is one of the largest US electrical distributors with a growing data center business.

EnerSys supplies UPS systems, batteries behind them, switchgear and integrated power solutions for data center, telecom and industrial customers, covering keeping power running. Every data center needs UPS and battery backup, but motive power and specialty batteries make up much of its sales. It is a major industrial battery maker with a meaningful but not leading position in data center backup.

Flex provides switchgear, busway, power distribution units, modular power systems and server power supplies for cloud and data center customers, covering distribution and power conversion. Demand grows with data center construction and power per rack, but contract manufacturing for many industries is most of Flex's business. Its data center power business is a significant and growing supplier.

Advanced Energy makes power conversion products, including DC-DC solutions and power supplies for servers and storage, alongside plasma power for semiconductor equipment. Rising power per rack and 800 V DC designs add demand for conversion, but semiconductor equipment power is a large part of its sales. It is a meaningful supplier of data center server power.

MasTec builds electrical transmission and distribution systems and installs power infrastructure through its Power Delivery segment, which is installing grid connection equipment. Grid connection work grows as data centers are built, but communications, clean energy and pipeline work make up much of MasTec's business. It is one of the larger US infrastructure contractors.

Primoris installs and maintains electrical transmission and distribution systems through its Utilities segment, alongside energy and pipeline work, which places it in installing grid connection. Grid connection work grows with data center buildout, but much of its business is gas, renewables EPC and pipelines. It is a mid-sized contractor with an indirect role in data center power.

American Superconductor supplies grid interconnection, power quality and reactive power systems, transformers and rectifiers to utilities and industrial customers. Grid connection and power quality are needed as large loads connect to the grid, but its wind and naval businesses are also significant. It is a small specialist with limited direct data center exposure.

Regal Rexnord makes alternators for prime and standby power used in data centers and switchgear for commercial and industrial settings, which is keeping power running and distribution. Backup power demand grows with data centers, but motors, power transmission and motion control are most of the business. It is a secondary supplier in data center backup power.

Navitas makes gallium nitride and silicon carbide power semiconductors for power conversion, used in data centers among other markets, which are the power chips in 800 V DC conversion equipment. 800 V DC designs add demand for these chips if they reach scale, though timing is unclear and mobile and consumer charging are a large share of current sales. It is a small company whose data center role rests on emerging designs.

Amphenol makes busbars and complete power distribution systems alongside its much larger connector business, which places it in distributing power inside the rack and site. Rising power per rack increases power distribution content, but connectors for data, automotive and industrial markets dominate its sales. It is a major data center interconnect supplier with a smaller power distribution role.

Power Integrations makes high-voltage power conversion ICs and gate drivers, including for HVDC, which are power chips used in conversion equipment. 800 V DC designs could add demand for high-voltage conversion chips, though when they reach scale is unclear and most of its sales are consumer and industrial. Its position in data center power is small today.

Littelfuse makes circuit protection, power control and power semiconductors used in power conversion and data centers among many markets. Distribution and protection content grows with power per rack, but automotive and industrial markets make up most of its sales. It is a secondary supplier in data center electrical equipment.

AMETEK makes power quality monitoring, metering, uninterruptible power supplies and programmable power equipment among a broad instrument portfolio. Power quality and UPS demand grows with data centers, but these are a small part of AMETEK's diversified business. It is a minor player in data center electrical equipment.

Analog Devices makes power management ICs used for power conversion among a broad analog chip portfolio, which places it among the power chip suppliers for conversion equipment. 800 V DC and denser racks add power conversion content, but data converters, amplifiers and RF dominate its business. Its role in data center electrical equipment is small relative to its size.

Legence designs and installs mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems for buildings including data centers, which makes it partly an electrical installer. Every data center needs systems installed, but HVAC and mechanical work are the larger part of what it does. It is a mid-sized building systems firm with data center customers.
